title: Training Note: Credit Base for a Driver Excluded from a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy
content:
When a household member is excluded from a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy, the credit base of the exclusion credit follows how the excluded driver was charged during the term.

## The rule

The excluded driver's addition is that driver's latest driver addition entry in the policy's transaction history, by effective date.

| How the excluded driver was charged | Credit base |
|---|---|
| The driver's addition carries an additional premium entry of the current term | The charge written on that entry times the credit days, divided by the days that charge was written for: the unearned share of what was actually charged |
| The driver was added during the term with a premium effect, but no additional premium entry was written | Nil: nothing was charged |
| Otherwise | The full-term charge of the excluded driver times the credit days, divided by the days of the exclusion's term |

**Days the charge was written for.** These are the calendar days to the term expiration date, counted from one of two dates:
- from the addition's effective date, where the addition was recorded no more calendar days after that effective date than the package's household driver report days;
- otherwise, from the date the addition was recorded.

The household driver report days are 30 on every package: Cardinal Auto Essential, Cardinal Auto Basic, Cardinal Auto Standard, Cardinal Auto Plus, Cardinal Auto Preferred and Cardinal Auto Premier.

"Added during the term" means the addition's effective date is on or after the term effective date. "With a premium effect" means the addition entry shows a premium effect other than none.

## Questions answered (hypothetical; term 1 January to 1 July 2026, 91 credit days)

**The driver was added effective 1 March 2026 and recorded 20 March (19 days, within 30). An additional premium entry of 240.00 was written. What is the credit base?**
The charge was written for the 122 days from 1 March to 1 July. The credit base is 240.00 times 91 divided by 122, which is 179.0163… (unrounded).

**The addition was instead effective 1 February 2026 and recorded 15 March (42 days, beyond 30)?**
The charge was written for the 108 days from 15 March to 1 July. The credit base is 240.00 times 91 divided by 108, which is 202.2222… (unrounded).

**The driver was added in the term with a premium effect, and no additional premium entry exists?**
The credit base is nil.

**The driver has been on the policy since before the term began?**
The credit base is the full-term charge of the excluded driver times 91, divided by 181.
